title: Tab-bearing cells use the wrong start column during alignment
symptom: The shared table engine measures a cell containing a tab as if the cell began at display column zero. Since tab stops depend on the actual starting column, the rebuilt separator or terminal columns can remain misaligned or wider than the measured minimum. A reproduced Python source is `a: X\t| Y = 1\nbb: Z | Y = 2\nccc: X | Y = 3`; expected separator columns are `:` at 4 and `=` at 12 after tab expansion. Additional cases cover mixed indentation, tabs inside quoted cells, prefix rows and trailing comments.

rootCause.summary: The original shared width and rebuild paths measured tab-bearing cells from display column zero instead of each slot start, causing incorrect boundaries at tab stops. Candidate v2 retains the bounded correction; the final 50-file audit and full check passed, and the Opus fix-only review passed. The issue remains limited to this mechanism and existing width policy.

requestedOutcome: Measure tab-bearing cells at their actual display start column and produce minimum aligned boundaries while preserving source tab bytes, indentation, comments, syntax, and second-pass idempotence.
decisions: Keep the existing display-width policy and preserve tab bytes; this issue does not decide a new tab width or Unicode-width policy.
Keep detector, minimum-row, refusal, approval, and public write contracts unchanged.
